titulo: From the district to the State
intro: How a country is divided, who represents it, and words for war, crime and belief that appear in every newspaper.
p.el Tercer Mundo.nota: Historical expression; avoid using it as a neutral label for countries today.
b1.texto:
**Territory.** Spain is divided into seventeen **comunidades autónomas** and fifty **provincias**. A big city is divided into **distritos** and **barrios**. **La nación**, **el Estado**, **el país**.

**Institutions.** **El Congreso** and **el Senado** form **el parlamento**. The government has **un presidente**, **vicepresidentes** and **ministros**: **de Interior**, **de Defensa**, **de Educación**, **de Asuntos Exteriores**. Abroad, a country has **una embajada** in the capital, with **un embajador**, and **consulados** in other cities, each with **un cónsul**. Beyond the country: **la Unión Europea (UE)** and **la ONU**.

**If you lose your passport** abroad, you go to **el consulado**.

**The army.** **Un soldado**, **un capitán**, **un general**: all are **militares**. **Una guerra civil**, **mundial**, **de independencia**. **Estar en guerra.** **Una pistola**, **una bomba**.

**Crime.** **Un ladrón** roba; **un asesino** mata; **un terrorista** commits **un atentado**. Something against the law **es ilegal**, and the guilty **van a la cárcel**.

**The world.** **Los países de ingresos altos / bajos**, **los países en desarrollo**, **la desigualdad** and **el progreso**. **Tercer Mundo** is a historical expression; avoid using it as a neutral label for countries today.

**Manners.** **La cortesía**, **la amabilidad**; **ser amable**, **ser buena persona**.

**Belief.** **Cristiano**, **católico**, **protestante**, **musulmán**, **judío**. **El sacerdote** says mass. **La Biblia**, **el Corán**. **El cielo** and **el infierno**.
b2.f0: On the last day of my trip to Morocco I lost my passport, or perhaps a very skilful thief stole it from me.
b2.f1: At the police station, an officer explained to me very kindly that I had to go to the consulate.
b2.f2: The embassy was in the capital, three hundred kilometres away, but there was a consulate in the very city I was in.
b2.f3: In front of the door there were two soldiers, and inside, a queue of people with the same problem.
b2.f4: The consul signed a temporary document so that I could return to Spain.
b2.f5: He told me I should check which documents I needed to return to Spain, and wished me a good journey.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, where did the traveller get a new document?
b4.o0.refuerzo: El cónsul firmó un documento provisional.
b4.o1.refuerzo: It was three hundred kilometres away.
b4.o2.refuerzo: They sent him to the consulate.
b5.o1.refuerzo: Those are parts of a city.
b6.pregunta: The Congreso and the Senado together form…
b6.o0.refuerzo: El parlamento is parliament, formed by the Congreso and the Senado together.
b6.o2.refuerzo: A dated expression; it is not a neutral label for a group of countries today.
b7.pregunta: Complete: he went to prison for five years.
b8.o0: They dealt with me very kindly.
b8.o1: They attended me with many friends.
b8.o2: They waited for me with much love.
b8.o2.explicacion: Atender: to deal with. Amabilidad: kindness.
b9.traduccion: I had to go to the consulate to ask for another passport.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Explain how your country is divided and governed, from the town to the State.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Tell aloud what you would do if you lost your passport abroad.
b8.o0.explicacion: Me atendieron means they served or dealt with me, and amabilidad means kindness.
